# Grapheme clusters

Extended grapheme cluster boundaries, and how many user-perceived characters a text holds.

<h2 id="is-grapheme-boundary"><code>IsGraphemeBoundary</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsGraphemeBoundary(text: char32[..], index: uint) -> bool
```

Whether a cluster boundary falls before `index` in `text`.
The ends count: position zero and the length are always boundaries, which is what makes "the clusters of a
text" a partition of it. The rules between are UAX #29's, applied to the pair either side of the position with
lookback where a rule reaches further — the emoji join, the flag pairs, and the Indic conjuncts.
Runs in time proportional to the lookback, which is the run of marks behind the position; allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Unicode/Src/Graphemes.rux#L83)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type         | Description                            |
| ------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `text`  | `char32[..]` | the scalar values to examine           |
| `index` | `uint`       | the position to test, in scalar values |

**Returns**: whether a grapheme cluster boundary falls before `index`

<h2 id="count-graphemes"><code>CountGraphemes</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CountGraphemes(text: char32[..]) -> uint
```

How many grapheme clusters `text` holds.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Unicode/Src/Graphemes.rux#L170)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type         | Description                |
| ------ | ------------ | -------------------------- |
| `text` | `char32[..]` | the scalar values to count |

**Returns**: how many grapheme clusters `text` holds
